imagePrompt: A modern, semi-realistic golf illustration (about 75% realistic and 25% stylised) in a parkland setting. Show one golfer on the course, looking at a golf ball that is clearly under a thick bush, with no way to play the ball out. The golfer's bag is resting nearby. The focus is on visualising the scenario where the ball is unplayable and the golfer is about to measure for lateral relief. Do not include text, labels, numbers, arrows, captions, diagrams, badges, logos, watermarks, club crests, scorecards or speech bubbles.
imageAlt: A golfer examines their golf ball lying under a bush, deciding how to take relief.

sceneSpec.setting: A parkland golf hole bordered by bushes and long grass.
sceneSpec.players: One golfer, shown deciding on their next action, with a bag resting nearby.
sceneSpec.ballPosition: The ball is clearly under a dense bush, partly visible.
sceneSpec.ruleMoment: Just before the player measures their lateral relief area to drop the ball.
sceneSpec.educationalFocus: Visualising the scenario when a ball is unplayable and lateral relief is chosen.
mustShow: A golfer assessing a ball under a thick bush.
A visible golf ball lodged under the bush.
The situation making further play impossible without relief.
mustNotShow: A dropped ball or any actual measurement.

questions.title: How far can you drop your ball if you can't play it?
questions.question: Your ball is stuck under a bush and you can't hit it. If you choose to drop it to the side, how far are you allowed to move away from where it was?
questions.explanation: If your ball cannot be played and you want to drop it to the side (lateral relief), you are allowed to drop it within two club-lengths from where your ball was, but not closer to the hole.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: This means you move the ball sideways (to the side), not closer to the hole, when you can't play it.
The length of your golf club, used to measure how far you can drop your ball.

questions.teachingTip: Show children how to lay two clubs down on the ground to measure two club-lengths from the ball.
likelyMisconceptions: Children might think you can drop anywhere you want away from the bush.
Children may think you can drop closer to the hole.
Some may believe 'nearest point you can play' means you can pick any spot you like.

questions.title: How far may you drop for lateral relief from an unplayable ball?
questions.question: Your ball is under a bush. You decide to declare it unplayable and take lateral relief. How far may you drop?
questions.explanation: When taking lateral relief for an unplayable ball, you must drop the ball within two club-lengths of where the ball lies, no nearer the hole.
